original_question: Suppose f is a polynomial with zeros Z(f) in the complement of the open unit disk D, and let q_n be the n-th optimal polynomial approximant of 1/f in H^2_omega. For which weights {omega_k}_{k in N} is it true that 1 - q_n f converges to 0 uniformly on compact subsets of D \ Z(f)?
target_in_paper: Open Question 6 in §5.2, posed immediately after Theorem 5.5 as the weighted-space extension of that pointwise/boundary convergence result. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right open problem, the right class of functions (polynomials with zeros outside the open unit disk), the right approximants (the n-th optimal polynomial approximant q_n to 1/f in H^2_ω), and the right qualitative conclusion to classify by the weight sequence, namely compact-uniform convergence of 1 - q_n f away from the zeros. It also correctly stays with polynomials rather than broadening to the separate non-polynomial question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
missing_details: The paper’s standing definition of the weighted Hardy space H^2_ω should be made explicit: it is a Hilbert space of analytic functions on the unit disk associated to a weight sequence ω = (ω_k) with the standing hypotheses introduced in §1.

The optimization defining q_n should be stated explicitly: q_n is the unique polynomial of degree at most n that minimizes ||1 - p f||_{H^2_ω} (equivalently ||p f - 1||_{H^2_ω}) over all polynomials p of degree at most n.
The ambient setting should be spelled out: the unit disk is D = {z in C : |z| < 1}, the coefficients are complex, and Z(f) denotes the zero set of f.
The quantifier over f should be explicit: the question is to characterize those weights for which the stated convergence holds whenever f is a polynomial whose zeros lie in the complement of D.

To match the nearby context in §5.2, the intended problem is the boundary-strengthened version modeled on Theorem 5.5, i.e. compact-uniform convergence away from the zeros up to the boundary, not merely the interior compact convergence that is discussed earlier as a consequence of norm convergence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
It should remain restricted to polynomials; the paper asks the broader non-polynomial variant separately as Open Question 7. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
refined_question: Under the paper’s standing assumptions on the weight sequence ω = (ω_k)_{k≥0} defining the weighted Hardy space H^2_ω, characterize those weights for which the following holds: whenever f is a complex polynomial whose zero set Z(f) lies in the complement of the open unit disk D = {z in C : |z| < 1}, and q_n is the unique polynomial of degree at most n minimizing ||1 - p f||_{H^2_ω} over all polynomials p of degree at most n, the errors 1 - q_n f converge uniformly to 0 on every compact subset of the closed unit disk that avoids Z(f).
justification: The draft is aimed squarely at Open Question 6, not at a broader neighboring problem. Section 1 supplies the standing notation for H^2_ω and for n-th optimal polynomial approximants, while §5 first distinguishes the already-known compact convergence inside the open disk from the harder boundary behavior, and then §5.2 records Theorem 5.5 before posing Open Question 6 as the natural extension to general weights. Because Open Question 7 separately asks about functions other than polynomials, the refined question should remain polynomial-only. The only substantial sharpening needed is to make the definitions and quantifiers explicit and to preserve the boundary-convergence intent of the surrounding discussion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
